title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages). X = D_0 is a space with a stratification at infinity; for the notes' purpose X is \bar M_{g,ν} with its Deligne–Mumford boundary, which is a normal crossings divisor in the stack sense. D_d is the normalized ('diplongé') closure of the codimension-d stratum, i.e. curves with at least d nodes, equipped with an ordering or choice of the local branches. For d ≥ d', D_{d,d'} is the corresponding incidence/fibre object: a point of D_d together with a choice of d' of its d branches. It maps to D_d and to D_{d'}. On each D_d Grothendieck has three objects. (i) A local system of free Z-modules T_d of rank d: the lattice indexed by the branches through the stratum, i.e. the cocharacters of the normal torus. (ii) The torus G_d = T_d ⊗_Z G_m. (iii) A G_d-torsor P_d: the product of the d normal line bundles minus their zero sections, the algebraic model of the deleted tubular neighbourhood. On D_{d,d'} he has: (194) a surjection of lattices T(d,d')_d → T(d,d')_{d'}; (197) the induced smooth epimorphism of tori G(d,d')_d → G(d,d')_{d'}; and (198) an isomorphism of torsors P(d,d')_{d'} ≃ P(d,d')_d ∧^{G_d} G_{d'}, i.e. change of structure group. Geometrically, the normal bundle of D_{d'} restricted to D_d is the quotient factor of the normal bundle of D_d corresponding to the d' chosen branches.

This page. For a triple d ≥ d' ≥ d'', he introduces D_{d,d',d''}. Pulling back T, G, P along the three projections to D_d, D_{d'}, D_{d''} gives (199)–(201). Pulling back the data (194), (197), (198) along the three projections to D_{d,d'}, D_{d',d''}, D_{d,d''} gives three morphisms in each case. These satisfy the transitivity (cocycle) relations (202): the composite d → d' → d'' equals the direct d → d'' map, for T, for G and for P. He remarks that all of these relations are essentially tautological. He then announces a non-tautological one, which uses the normal crossings hypothesis 'in its two forms'.

The next page shows what that relation is. The stratification induced on each D_d again comes from a normal crossings divisor, so one has open complements D*_d and D*_{d,d'}. From this he obtains canonical 'generalization' homomorphisms π_1 P*_d → π_1 P*_{d'} for d' < d. These are homomorphisms between the fundamental groups of the deleted tubular neighbourhoods of the strata, i.e. between the boundary or 'at infinity' fundamental groups.

Purpose. To set up the combinatorial-geometric skeleton (lattices, tori, torsors, and their compatibility over iterated incidence varieties) needed to describe the 'structure at infinity' of M_{g,ν]. That means the system of fundamental groups of the tubular neighbourhoods of boundary strata, together with their specialization and generalization maps. This structure governs the Teichmüller tower and Galois actions at tangential base points.
errors: No mathematical error. Grothendieck himself rightly calls the transitivities (202) tautological: they follow from the transitivity of branch choices and from functoriality of pull-back and of change of structure group.

Implicit, unwritten point: the cocycle identity for P is really an identity between isomorphisms of torsors, (P_d ∧ G_{d'}) ∧ G_{d''} ≃ P_d ∧ G_{d''}. The associativity constraint of contracted products is used silently; this is harmless.

In the M_{g,ν} case the strata are stacks and branches can be permuted (self-intersection of the boundary divisor). This is why the 'diplongement' D_d with ordered or chosen branches is needed. The page handles this implicitly through the indices and does not spell it out.

ideas.what: Over the d-th boundary stratum: a rank-d lattice local system T_d, the normal torus G_d = T_d⊗G_m, and the G_d-torsor P_d (punctured normal bundle), as the model of the deleted tubular neighbourhood
ideas.modern_name: Torus-torsor description of a normal crossings / toroidal boundary; essentially the characteristic sheaf of the log structure and its associated G_m^d-torsor (Kato–Nakayama / log geometry, deformation to the normal cone)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Toroidal embeddings: Kempf–Knudsen–Mumford–Saint-Donat (1973). Log structures: Fontaine–Illusie, K. Kato (late 1980s). Kato–Nakayama spaces (1999)
ideas.where_published: The 'structure à l'infini' and tubular neighbourhoods of the strata of M_{g,n} are evoked qualitatively in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this formalism is not there

ideas.what: Transitivity (cocycle) relations for the lattice, torus and torsor maps over the triple incidence variety D_{d,d',d''}
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality and transitivity of cospecialization maps of the characteristic monoid of a log structure; compatibility of normal-cone data in a stratified space
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in log geometry and toroidal geometry

ideas.what: Announced generalization homomorphisms π_1 P*_d → π_1 P*_{d'} between fundamental groups of deleted tubular neighbourhoods of strata, built from the normal crossings hypothesis (developed on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Specialization/generalization maps between boundary (tangential-base-point) fundamental groups; exit-path or stratified fundamental groupoid at infinity of \bar M_{g,n}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara–Nakamura (1997); H. Nakamura's work on Galois actions at infinity of M_{g,n}; Hoshi–Mochizuki on combinatorial anabelian geometry; exit paths (MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses tangential base points and the role of boundary strata only in outline

missed.claim: The system (T_d, G_d, P_d) with transitivity data over the iterated incidence varieties D_{d,d',d''} is in substance a hand-built version of the characteristic sheaf of the log structure of \bar M_{g,ν}, with its cospecialization maps and the associated torus torsors (the algebraic counterpart of the Kato–Nakayama space). It is organized around the normalized strata rather than a sheaf of monoids. This is a mild historical precursor rather than a new result.
missed.quote: on a plusieurs du type (194), (197), (198), et donc des transitivités
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of historical interest: it documents Grothendieck independently setting up log-geometric data for the boundary of moduli of curves as the base for his 'structure at infinity' programme. The mathematics itself is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is bookkeeping: pull-backs to the triple incidence variety and cocycle conditions that Grothendieck himself calls tautological. The non-trivial step (generalization maps on π_1 of punctured tubular neighbourhoods) is only announced here and carried out on the next page.
transcription_corrections: Lines 3–4: the crossed-out symbols are the subscripted D_d, D_{d'}, D_{d''} (written 'D(d)_d' etc. and struck through). The sentence reads 'des quantités correspondantes sur [D_d, D_{d'}, D_{d''}] par'.
'Prenant par ⇒' is likely 'Prenant par ailleurs' (the scribble after 'par' is an abbreviation, not an implication arrow).
'on a plusieurs du type' probably reads 'on a [des] (relations/morphismes) du type (194), (197), (198)'; the words are ambiguous in the image.
In (201) the first item is P(d,d',d'')_d (the image shows 'P(d,d'd'')_d' with a missing comma); the third is P(d,d',d'')_{d''}.
